commentary_segments.text: The noise voltage is measured at the output of the analog amplifier structure. It is clear that the singleended amplifier is much more sensitive to the digital noise than the fully-differential one. Increasing the supply voltage increases the currents in the logic gates and also the spike current transfer to the analog circuits. This is clearly visible on the right. Even the differential noise pick up increases rather drastically. This is probably due to mismatch in substrate contacts. Quite often many sources of mismatch are often overlooked. For example for a fully-differential input stage of an opamp, good matching not only requires perfectly symmetrical layout but also identical surroundings. For example, the substrate contacts of the input transistors must also have the same size and an equal distance to the axis of symmetry. If not, different substrate resistances result, and different body effects.
